Alice M: Quick observation from today's load run — we saw a bunch of partial-decode bursts when stream clients hit token caps. tail p99 latency jumped ~3x for 200ms windows.
Ben K: ugh. which config was in prod? token_budget=64? batch_window_ms=15?
Alice M: Prod had token_budget=64, batch_target=48, coalesce_ms=12. Kernel selector change yesterday switched small-kernel preference for short sequences, that might explain the perf cliff.
Caroline J: Did we see KV cache warmup miss spikes too? that makes partial-decode worse if kv lookup stalls.
Alice M: Yes — KV cache heatmap shows a spike in misses around the same time range (logs attached). Miss rate went from 2% -> 9% across hosts.
Ravi P: I ran a quick trace. Pattern: many short requests get coalesced into micro-batches, but when token_budget timer fires we send partials out. The small-kernel uses less kernel-latency for single token, but causes more preemption when batch forms.
Ben K: So two interacting things: kernel choice altered per-request op cost, and the token_budget/flush cadence now triggers earlier partial sends. We should smooth the token_budget deadline relative to batch formation.
Caroline J: Proposal: move from a fixed token_budget deadline per request to a sliding token_budget that's aligned with batch_head_age percentiles. Pseudoconfig: 
```
batch_window_ms: 12
sliding_token_budget_ms_percentile: 80
token_budget_min: 32
token_budget_max: 128
prefetch_factor: 1.25
```
Alice M: Also add a small jitter to partial-send deadlines to avoid synchronized flush storms: +rand(0..3ms) on deadline. That alone reduced microburst overlap in sim.
Ravi P: On kernel selection: add a cheap cost-estimate step using recent observed kernel latency per sequence length bucket. If small-kernel shows variance >20% under load, prefer stable medium-kernel for coalesced batches.
Ben K: Can we add an exponential backoff for partial-decode requeues? If a request partial-sent but then immediately needs more tokens, we should try to coalesce its next tokens for up to 4ms instead of immediately sending another micro-partial.
Caroline J: I prototyped in staging: changes combined -> p99 drops 35%, median unchanged, overall token-efficiency +6%. CPU/kernel switches reduced by ~18%. KV-miss mitigation: prefetch_factor bumped from 1.0 to 1.25 gave much smoother KV hit curves.
devinfra-bot: deploy:staging v2026.03.01-tiling-prefetch rolled to canary(10%) at 2354007880 by Ben K
Alice M: Logs from staging run: 
```
[2354007901] batch_formed=12 avg_batch_size=5 token_budget_deadline_ms=28 jitter_ms=2 p99_latency_ms=112
[2354007906] batch_formed=9 avg_batch_size=6 token_budget_deadline_ms=31 jitter_ms=1 p99_latency_ms=78
[2354007918] kv_miss_rate=2.8% prefetch_factor=1.25 kernel_switches=5
```
Ravi P: We should monitor kernel switch count and correlated p99; if kernel_switches/second > threshold -> revert to stable kernel routing policy.
Ben K: Action items: 1) ramp config in staging to 50% by EOD, 2) add metric kernel_switches_per_min, kernel_latency_variance, sliding_token_budget_q80, 3) run 20m high-concurrency replay. I'll take 1+2. Alice take 3?
Alice M: I'm on the replay. Will post results to this thread.
Caroline J: If staging looks good, we can ship to prod with a 10% canary and 30m observation window. :thumbsup:
Ben K: Thanks — big win if we can avoid partial-decode storms without hurting throughput.
Alice M: FYI repro script: `./tools/replay --scenario=stream-burst --concurrency=1200 --seed=42 --short-seq-ratio=0.62`
Ravi P: + please add an alert: sliding_token_budget_q80 > 40ms AND p99_latency > 250ms -> paging oncall.
Alice M: noted. will add alert rules.
Caroline J: Also add a small eval to check generation quality after switching kernels (some hallucination edgecases on small kernel observed earlier).
Ben K: Good call. Might be subtle.
Alice M: OK closing for now, will update when replay finishes. :sparkles:
